activity.title: I'm wrapping up my internship at LinkedIn next week! It feels like I literally closed my eyes, and 12 weeks went by just like that. From having to learn completely new technical skills to getting to attend awesome intern events, I really couldn't have asked for a better summer. I think the thing that really makes LinkedIn a special place to intern is getting the chance to have chats with all the talented engineers here. Truly, I think I've learned more about distributed systems, databases, and proofs for how they work this summer than I have all of my undergrad. Sadly though, all good things must come to an end. With a single week left, I will now be wrapping up my project and attending the last LinkedIn intern party. It was truly an unforgettable summer.

Last week was LinkedIn's Company Kickoff event (CKO)! The CKO series was a three-day event where LinkedIn employees from different office branches flew in to hear about the company’s vision, leadership priorities, and goals for the upcoming year! Though I decided to exclude footage from the leadership talks themselves (gotta be careful), I put together a video showing what the event was like outside! #LinkedIn #Internship #SWE #Tech #LinkedInLife #LinkedInterns

Here’s how a random connection led to me getting my first big tech internship. One day long ago in the prehistoric age of 2024, I connected with Daniel Fu . As I peeped his profile, something interesting caught my eye. That was the CodePath Internship Connection Program. One thing led to another, and I applied to the program. Eventually, this led to me getting connections and landing roles over at Bentley Systems and BILL. But here’s the thing, none of this would have ever happened if I didn't stumble upon his profile, which is kinda scary to think about (I have no clue where I'd be today without it 😭). So, my take on this story is to always connect with others and see if you can learn something new to succeed! May the LinkedIn algorithm be in your favor 🙏. #LinkedIn #Internship #SWE #Tech #LinkedInLife #LinkedInterns

Finally passed 300,000 impressions 🙈 I first started posting last year and was never really too big on sharing stories on the platform, but boy oh boy did I have a change of heart. My first post to make it big was my post on "how I landed my first internship". Since then I’ve made 15 other posts sharing all of the other stuff I’ve been up to during my undergrad. LinkedIn is a pretty interesting platform in that you never really know what’s gonna explode, but for those starting out, my biggest advice is to post every fairly so often so you don’t fall off. If you have anything interesting to share, post about it. Could be something as small as sharing how you overcame a deviously hard class or made a cool project. #LinkedIn #Internship #SWE #Tech #LinkedInLife #LinkedInterns

Today’s my last day of the LinkedIn company shutdown break! So I wanted to make a small homage post on all of the fun stuff I’ve done so far! On day one, we had onboarding and got to learn more about the company history and culture, and of course got our LinkedIn swag! A few weeks after, we got a visit from some puppies (they were very very cute and soft, 10/10 experience). The next week, a Family Feud game show showdown (was fun seeing interns compete in triva!). Next came the company fair, many booths were placed right outside B7 and I got to play some fun fair games with my team, pet some bunnies, and eat some corn dogs! There was also the Intern InDay event, which was another 10/10. Got to learn about the different ERG groups and bring home my self-made BBQ spice. The insane thing is that these aren’t even all the events LinkedIn’s had. I left out a lot of other events that I wasn’t able to go to like the baseball game and the hiking trip. I really do have to lock IN and go to more stuff though for the remaining 5 weeks! #LinkedIn #Internship #SWE #Tech #LinkedInLife #LinkedInterns

Another summer, another grind, and another internship wrap-up post :) This one is for my summer as a SWE intern at Capital One this summer. Week one was onboarding at the Richmond campus. A lot of sessions about how the company works, and a lot of new names I definitely did not remember by Friday. Then I got to headquarters in McLean and met my team on Small Business Card. That week is where things started to change for me. I got to see how a company with millions of users actually ships. Feature toggles so you can shut a change off before customers ever notice, tests that actually hold up, CI/CD, and a lot of process I had never seen. The infrastructure was intimidating at first, but I slowly got the hang of it. 😅 My project was modernizing key UI elements for our small business credit card users and shipping new features that show customers clearer info about their account declines. Halfway through, I took a 48-hour break for the intern hackathon. My team built a platform that stops sensitive data from leaking into AI tools, and we won 1st place out of 100+ interns. Outside of all the code, one of my favorite parts was connecting with the full-timers and attending all the cool intern events like Kings Dominion amusement park, Punch Social, and just the random intern shenanigans. A huge thank you to my teammates who made this summer: Philip Chryssochoos , Pranav Raghavan , Reagan Gary , Reet Kaler , and Rishan Biju . And a huge thank you to my manager Emma Sona for the guidance and support all summer. You all made this summer. Now it's back to Tampa to make the most out of my final semester!

I helped organize the Glades Teacher Appreciation Breakfast event, honoring our local teachers and their dedication to ensuring academic success for their students! Today, over 200 teachers and staff attended the event. Eleven teachers were recognized as GEMAD (Glades Educators Making a Difference) award recipients, an honor presented by The Hand Foundation to recognize an outstanding educator from each school in the Glades every year. I had the opportunity to dive deep into logistics and budgeting, vendor sourcing, event marketing, and putting my design skills to work by creating event pamphlets, all to ensure the morning was truly special for everyone. I'm so grateful to The Hand Foundation for allowing me to take part in such a meaningful event and support our local community. As a former student, I deeply appreciate the support I received from my teachers, from KEC/Canal Point Elementary to Pahokee Middle-Senior High School, because it shaped me into who I am today. High school brought some of the toughest times in my life due to personal and health challenges. Even though I was one of the quietest students in class and never talked about these issues, my teachers made sure I never went unnoticed. I may not have had the chance to thank every teacher who showed up with kindness, empathy, and encouragement during those moments, but I carry that gratitude with me. To every educator reading this: thank you for everything you do, for always cheering us on, and for being like family to your students. Your impact creates lasting, positive change! Being able to give back to the community I grew up in has been incredibly meaningful. One of my proudest milestones this summer was helping secure funding for a special local organization close to my heart; stay tuned to hear who! :) #GEMAD #TheHandFoundation #GladesCommunity #GivingBack #TeacherAppreciation

A couple of big announcements! First, I’m excited to share that this May, I graduated from the University of Rochester with a B.A. in Computer Science. In addition to the many professional and academic skills I gained throughout college, my education taught me to be resilient, curious, optimistic, and forward-looking. I’m incredibly grateful to all the friends, professors, and family members who supported me on this journey. Second, I’m excited to announce that today I am starting a new position as an Associate Software Engineer at Visa ! I’m deeply grateful for the opportunity to work at a company of such scale, where I can combine my interests in finance and software engineering. My life has been connected to Visa since my teenage years: my first debit card was a Visa card, and my first purchase in the United States was made with a Visa card. Now, I get to contribute to the company that has supported me throughout my life by helping make payments easy and accessible everywhere. A special thanks to Dana Hestand for bringing me to the company and supporting me throughout the recruiting process and Krishnan Nair for having me on the team. #LifeAtVisa #ComputerScience , #SoftwareEngineering , #NewGrad
